_note: M2 blessed golden set. Demand + ABC/XYZ derived INDEPENDENTLY of the engine from REAL historical DO order_lines in the local prod-copy DB (see _derivation). Demand is bucketed WEEKLY (~13 x 7-day buckets over the 90-day window) so CV + the 10% trim are meaningful. Supplier golden numbers are hand-computed from a synthetic PO/GR fixture built inside each test's savepoint (see test_m2_supplier_perf.py). Assert engine output within tolerance on rates/baseline, exact on class letters/method.

_derivation.buckets: ~13 trailing 7-day (weekly) buckets over the 90-day window ending exclusively at as_of=2026-06-01. Bucket index = floor((as_of - order_date - 1)/7), newest-first: index 0 = the most recent 7 days [2026-05-25,2026-06-01); the oldest bucket (index 12) is the short remainder clamped to the 90-day window start. Bucket demand = SUM(order_lines.quantity) over non-cancelled orders in the week (same rows as scm.consumption_v). The `buckets` array below is newest-first. See scripts/scm_m2_golden_derive.py.
_derivation.avg_daily_demand: baseline_total / window_days (90). For method 'mean' baseline_total == total (sum of all weekly buckets). For 'trimmed_mean' (Y band only) baseline_total == kept_mean * num_buckets where kept_mean drops the top+bottom 10% of the 13 weekly totals (floor(0.10*13)=1 period each tail).
_derivation.demand_cv: population sigma/mu of the 13 per-bucket DAILY RATES (bucket_qty / bucket_days), statistics.pstdev / mean, ddof=0. Rates (not raw totals) so the short 6-day oldest bucket does not structurally inflate variability (S3); buckets 0..11 are 7-day weeks, bucket 12 is the 6-day remainder.
_derivation.method: Trim ONLY the moderate-variability Y band: 'trimmed_mean' when 0.5<demand_cv<=1.0 (drops one weekly period off each tail so an occasional spike week no longer inflates the baseline); otherwise 'mean'. Both the steady X band (cv<=0.5) AND the lumpy Z band (cv>1.0) use the plain mean (baseline==total) — a single-spike Z SKU must NOT be trimmed to a zero baseline; its Z class letter already flags low confidence.
_derivation.xyz_class: X when cv<=0.5, Y when cv<=1.0, Z when cv>1.0 (abc_xyz_policy xyz_x_max=0.5, xyz_y_max=1.0). Weekly bucketing raises CV vs the old 30-day buckets, so lumpy SKUs now classify Y/Z. The XYZ band drives the trim decision so the branch and the class letter always agree.
_derivation.abc_class: Rank ALL costed (product.cost_price>0) SKU x warehouse keys by trailing-365-day annual value SUM(qty*cost_price) desc; class decided on the cumulative share of grand total BEFORE the item itself is added (prev_cum): A when prev_cum<=80%, B when prev_cum<=95%, C=rest (abc_xyz_policy abc_a_pct=80, abc_b_pct=95). This is the standard ABC rule (B1): the boundary-crossing item belongs to the HIGHER class and rank-1 (prev_cum=0) is ALWAYS A. FT-03 sits astride the 80% cut (cum 80.67 / prev_cum 79.16) so it classes A, not B. Null-cost keys => abc_class null (unknown).

channel_split_sku._note: cont(152)+untagged(798) default to continuous=950; spike=150; sum=total=1100 (no double-count). Window totals are independent of bucket width.
